title: Implement BZK09 §3 salient curvature directions for FaceRosyField
description:
PATCH-95 H2 cross-field investigation: our metriko-baseline data has 32 singularities (16 each of index plus/minus 1) on rocker-arm vs Lyon paper's 36. Lyon section 7 lines 473-481: Lyon used Bommes-Zimmer-Kobbelt 2009 (BZK09) Mixed-Integer Quadrangulation with Campen-Ibing-Ebke-Zorin-Kobbelt 2016 (CIE16) directional constraints. Our FaceRosyField + MiGreedyRounding implements BZK09 sections 2 + 4 (the angle-based MIQ formulation and greedy round-and-resolve solver) but NOT section 3 (Salient Curvature Directions), which detects high-anisotropy curvature regions and adds them as directional constraints. Our default constructor uses principalThreshold = POSITIVE_INFINITY which disables constraints entirely; the comment explicitly notes 'v1 keeps it disabled per the ticket.' Without constraints, the smoothness energy minimizer is under-determined (constant theta shift leaves energy unchanged), and singularity placements depend on mesh topology rather than curvature features. BZK09 section 3 algorithm: per-point compute shape operators S_r at multi-radii r in [r0, r1], where r0 = avg edge length, r1 = h target edge length, w = h/4 window. A shape operator is valid if all S_r in [r-w, r+w] have anisotropy tau = (|kappa_max| - |kappa_min|) / |kappa_max| above tau_min = 0.8 AND mean curvature above K = 0.1 / b_s (bounding-sphere radius). Among valid candidates per point, pick the most stable one (smallest angle deviation in interval). Add directional constraint at that face. Implementation steps: (a) compute per-face principal directions via shape operator estimation (Cohen-Steiner Morvan 2003 normal cycle), (b) apply anisotropy + curvature thresholds, (c) wire selected directions into MiGreedyRounding as fixed-theta constraints. Optional refinement: CIE16 scale-invariant alignment (separate paper, separate ticket).

UPDATE 2026-05-01: Simplified BZK09 section 3 implemented and shipped.

WHAT LANDED:
- MiGreedyRounding.setDirectionalConstraints(thetaPerFace, constrained) — pass per-face theta constraints with corresponding active flags. Applied via penalty in solveRelaxed() and fallback().
- FaceRosyField.applyCurvatureConstraints(greedy) — when principalThreshold is finite, computes per-face theta constraint from per-vertex PrincipalDirectionField (Meyer-style 1-ring shape operator), filters by anisotropy threshold tau >= principalThreshold, projects bestV-dirMax onto face local frame.
- Default constructor still uses POSITIVE_INFINITY = constraints disabled = legacy behavior preserved.
- New test: subdividedSphereWithCurvatureConstraintsStillStable verifies opt-in path on uniform sphere (anisotropy = 0 everywhere, no constraints fire).

REGRESSION: 92/92 quadlayout tests green (added 1 new test).

REMAINING WORK (not in this PR):
- Multi-radius shape operator per BZK09 section 3 paragraph 4-5 (we use single 1-ring; BZK09 uses multi-radius windowed search). Would handle mesh-scale variation better.
- Mean-curvature threshold K = 0.1/b_s (we use only anisotropy tau).
- CIE16 scale-invariant directional alignment refinement (separate paper).
- Empirical verification on rocker-arm requires either a faster MiGreedyRounding (currently times out on 20K faces) or a smaller paper-comparable mesh.

PATCH-96 STATUS: simplified version shipped, legacy preserved, opt-in via principalThreshold parameter. Multi-radius and CIE16 follow-ups deferred.
definition-of-done: FaceRosyField with principal-direction constraints enabled produces a cross-field whose singularity count on rocker-arm at default parameters approaches Lyon paper's 36 (currently 32 without constraints). Constraints are wired through the existing principalThreshold parameter. Default behavior remains constraints-disabled (POSITIVE_INFINITY) to preserve current tests; opt-in via constructor or CLI flag.
testing-plan: 1) Run our FaceRosyField on rocker-arm with no constraints; record singularity count (expect ~32, matching metriko-precomp). 2) Implement BZK09 §3 salient direction detection using shape operators per face. 3) Wire constraints into MiGreedyRounding. 4) Re-run rocker-arm with constraints enabled; verify sing count moves toward 36. 5) Quadlayout regression green.
